questions.q: How do simple exponential smoothing, Holt's method and Holt-Winters relate to each other?
options: They are three unrelated algorithms
Each adds a component: SES tracks a level, Holt adds a trend, and Holt-Winters adds a seasonal pattern
Holt-Winters removes the level and keeps only the season
SES adds a season, Holt removes it
questions.explain: The three methods build on one another: level, then level plus trend, then level plus trend plus seasonality.

questions.q: In the lesson, simple exponential smoothing fitted alpha = 1.0 and scored the same MAE as the naive baseline. Why?
options: With alpha = 1, only the most recent value counts, so the forecast is just the last observation repeated
Alpha = 1 averages all history equally
statsmodels ignores alpha for daily data
The model was fitted on the test set
questions.explain: The smoothing level alpha sets how much weight the newest point gets. At 1.0 the level equals the last value, which is exactly the naive forecast.

questions.q: What does the d in ARIMA(p, d, q) control?
options: How many past forecast errors are used
The number of forecast days
How many lagged values are regressed on
How many times the series is differenced to remove trend and make it more stationary
questions.explain: p is the autoregressive order, d the differencing order, and q the moving-average order on past errors.

questions.q: A plain ARIMA(1,1,1) scored worse than the baselines on the weekly sales series, while a seasonal version scored far better. What is the lesson?
options: ARIMA never beats baselines
Seasonal terms only work for monthly data
The model must be told about the seasonality (here a period of 7); otherwise it cannot capture the weekly cycle
Adding parameters always makes a model worse
questions.explain: Non-seasonal ARIMA has no term for a repeating weekly pattern. Setting seasonal_order with m = 7 lets it model the cycle.

questions.q: Why does the lesson choose the ARIMA order by AIC rather than by test-set MAE?
options: AIC is always smaller than MAE
AIC is computed on the training data and penalises extra parameters, so it does not use the test set to make the choice
The test set has no MAE
AIC is required by statsmodels
questions.explain: Selecting a model by its test error uses the test data to tune the model, which leaks information and makes the final score too optimistic.
